candidates.evidence: Full text read from the Diario Oficial PDF: https://www.diariooficial.interior.gob.cl/publicaciones/2026/03/26/44410/01/2782619.pdf . Amendment of 29 Jul 2026: https://www.diariooficial.interior.gob.cl/publicaciones/2026/07/29/44511/01/2843479.pdf (seen in search results and not read in full; summarised via search). Enforcement context: SAG draft decree replacing the 1983 fairs regulation (May 2026 draft: https://www.sag.cl/sites/default/files/BORRADOR-DECRETO-FERIAS-2026--mayo-2026-observaciones-afech_final.pdf). The 2019 predecessor Res. 7.782 gave 1 year to install RFID reading.
candidates.existing: Only the free official SIPEC module and SAG's 2016 'Titular Movimientos Ferias' manual. The targeted Spanish competitor search ('software feria ganadera remate recinto ferial Chile SIPEC') found no Chilean auction/feria software; only Ecuadorian academic projects. RFID reader hardware vendors not checked.
candidates.known_note: Same livestock-movement family as K08 (horse paperwork) but a different buyer group and a different duty.
candidates.name: Livestock-fair (recinto ferial) traceability and RFID desk: SIPEC movement upload, FMA matching, DIIO capture
candidates.trigger: SAG Res. Ex. 1.884/2026 (DO 26 Mar 2026), amended by Res. 6.589/2026 (DO 29 Jul 2026). Ferias may not receive or auction animals without the FMA. They must load entry and exit movements into the SIPEC Modulo Movimiento en Recintos Feriales within 3 business days of the auction, and carry-over animals by the day before the next auction. Bovines without an RFID DIIO cannot be received or sold. Ferias must have an electronic DIIO reading system and capture DIIO numbers electronically through the whole intake/exit flow. Paper FMAs go to the SAG office within 72 business hours. Ferias may print outgoing FMAs from their own systems if they meet the spec. Sanctions under the DFL RRA 16/1963 and Ley 18.755 and 19.162.
candidates.unchecked: Number and ownership of ferias; whether SAG gives free upload templates or RFID reader integration; transition period after the July 2026 amendment; whether big ferias (e.g. cooperative-run or Fegosa-type firms) already have in-house software; willingness to pay; whether a hardware-plus-software bundle is the real need.

candidates.evidence: SII resolution read: https://www.sii.cl/normativa_legislacion/resoluciones/2016/reso86.pdf . https://www.reporteminero.cl/noticia/noticias/2026/05/pdi-incauta-5-toneladas-cobre-robo-atacama-copiapo . https://www.reporteminero.cl/noticia/noticias/2026/01/aduanas-incauta-chatarra-cobre-ilegal-puerto-arica-destino-corea-del-sur . https://www.mch.cl/el-millonario-negocio-de-la-chatarra-de-cobre-en-la-mira-del-sii/ . candidates.existing: Competitor search ('software chatarrería Chile compra de chatarra factura de compra SII control proveedores sistema gestión') found no scrap-specific software in Chile; only SII resolutions and Codelco tenders.
candidates.name: Scrap-yard compliance pack: IVA withholding-agent status, origin documentation and supplier checks
candidates.trigger: SII Res. Ex. 86/2016 (total change of IVA taxpayer on scrap sales): companies that buy or sell scrap and are not exporters/manufacturers become withholding agents once monthly purchases or sales exceed CLP 20m net, or purchases reach CLP 150m net in 12 months. Withholding agents are listed in a public SII nomina and file the annex declarations. Enforcement is rising: PDI seized over 5 t of copper cable in Copiapo in May 2026 from a yard with no municipal permit, no start-of-activities and no origin documents (receptacion plus Ley REP offences); customs stopped suspected stolen copper scrap in Arica in Jan 2026; unions say only about 10% of yards are inspected.
candidates.unchecked: Rest of the SII resolution (annex forms, nomina rules, deadlines); number of yards over the thresholds; whether a mandatory registry bill advances in 2026-27; whether buyers will pay, since many yards are informal; legal risk of serving yards that launder stolen copper.

coverage.found: SSR operator registry deadline passed (Ley 21.520 extended to 20 Nov 2024); licences now being granted by decree with duties (Fondo de Reserva de Garantia, Fondo de Reposicion y Reinversion, e.g. DO 16 Dec 2025); tariff-fixing regulation DO 25 Feb 2026; Senate bill to modernise Ley 20.998 pending (May-Jun 2026). No periodic SISS report found; SSR run by MOP Subdireccion, not SISS. SSR management side stays K14 (APR Software/Octocelio). New angle found: water-right regularisation under Ley 21.435 (see candidate).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers (Ley Karin 21.643 / harassment protocol)
coverage.found: Ley Karin in force since 1 Aug 2024 and applies to every employer including micro firms (protocol, complaint channel, training). DT enforcement active (PwC: 2,117 inspections, 993 fines to Jun 2025; fines 3-60 UTM; dictamen 474/2025). But Rex+, Buk, Talana, Nubox already sell complaint-channel/protocol tools. Security/cleaning agencies otherwise still covered by K01/K02/K04/K10.

coverage.category: 31. Electrical/gas installers filing declarations to SEC (TE1, TC6) beyond net billing K05
coverage.found: TE1 (electrical, DS 8/2019 RIC) and TC6 (gas interior) are mandatory per-installation filings via SEC e-Declarador by licensed installers (credentials issued in person at SEC office; response 10 working days per ChileAtiende). SEC resolution on a new electronic procedure in e-Declarador published DO Sept 2025 (content unchecked). No Chilean installer software integrated with e-Declarador found; the state portal is the filing channel.

coverage.category: 20. Small food producers, restaurants, Seremi sanitary authorisation (DS 977) (gap)
coverage.found: Authorisation via free Seremi en Linea; DS 977 amended by Decreto 40/2024 (DO 25 Apr 2024; structural changes need authorisation, easier re-use of authorised premises); consolidated text amended to Jun 2025. Carnet de manipulador claim comes only from commercial training sites. No national food-handler registry found. No Chilean-specific HACCP/logbook tool found, only generic foreign apps. No recurring filing identified, mostly one-off authorisation plus inspections.

coverage.category: 22/30. Fruit packing, orchards, SAG registers (huertos exportadores, packing, cold stores) (gap)
coverage.found: SAG Sistema de Registro Agricola (Res. 7550/2021) is the official system where producers, packers, storage plants and exporters register, declare BPA/BPM/HACCP certifications and sign Acuerdos Operacionales de Inocuidad. Market-specific registers (Russia exporter list with 2026 commitment letter; raspberries; US citrus; Mexico stone fruit). No evidence found of annual renewal for SRA, nor counts of small registrants. No Chilean software linked to SRA found.

result.competitor: No Chilean commercial feria or auction software was found in searches in Spanish or English. Only foreign academic projects turned up (Ecuador, Colombia). SIPEC and its feria module are free from SAG. Big operators (Tattersall, Feria Osorno/Fegosa, cooperatives) have had to read DIIOs electronically since about 2020 and very likely have in-house or integrator systems, though I could not confirm this. RFID reader vendors (wand-to-PC to SIPECweb) were not checked.
result.duty: Confirmed in force. The texts below were seen through search-result summaries; the fetched Diario Oficial PDF was not machine-readable. Res. Ex. SAG 1.884/2026 (DO 26 Mar 2026) says ferias may not receive or auction animals without a paper or electronic FMA. Entry and exit movements go into the SIPEC Módulo Movimiento en Recintos Feriales within at most 3 business days after the auction (the Nov 2025 draft said 2 days), and before the next auction's intake. The amendment (DO 29 Jul 2026) replaces resuelvo 8: bovines without an RFID DIIO cannot be received or auctioned, and the official RFID DIIO number must be recorded in the module. It took effect on publication. The duty recurs with every auction, often weekly. Penalties are under the sanctions laws named in the claim (not re-verified). Electronic reading was already required within 1 year under Res. 7.782/2019.
result.market: The SAG BIOSIF reports count 42 recintos feriales in 2010, 41 in 2012, 39 in 2013, 38 in 2015, 39 in 2016 and 37 in 2017. The 2017 count includes 10 in Araucanía, 7 in Los Lagos and 6 in Maule. Eleven closed in the decade to 2016. No count after 2017 was found. AFECH (the ferias trade association) exists, but I did not find how many ferias it groups. Many ferias belong to a few larger firms.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. SAG Res. Ex. 1.884/2026 and its 29 Jul 2026 amendment require ferias to hold the FMA before receiving animals, load SIPEC movements within 3 business days and refuse bovines without an RFID DIIO. I found no third-party feria software, but the market is tiny. SAG BIOSIF reports counted about 37 recintos feriales in 2017, down from 42 in 2010. Large firms such as Tattersall and Feria Osorno/Fegosa run many of them. Electronic DIIO reading has been mandatory since Res. 7.782/2019, so working ferias likely already have in-house or integrator systems (unverified). SIPEC itself is free. That leaves very few buyers, a hardware-heavy integration and an established workflow: a weak solo-founder opportunity.

result.competitor: No Chilean software found that does the balance book or the SAG report for veterinary sellers. Two searches in Spanish found only regulation pages. The vet practice tools the discovery pass named (Veti.app, AgendaPro, etc.) were not re-checked.
result.duty: Res. 667/2010, which the claim cites, was repealed by SAG Res. Ex. 7813/2017 (14-12-2017, ketamine). Both facts come from the norm's title, seen in search summaries; I could not open the full text (LeyChile did not load, and the SAG and FAOLEX PDFs were unreadable). Under 7813, a search summary puts the monthly register sent to the SAG Subdepartamento de Registro y Control (first 10 business days) in the laboratory/importer section. Whether it binds sellers is not confirmed. 7813 limits ketamine sales to sellers registered with SAG and bans direct sale to vets. SAG still publishes lists of 'receta retenida con control de saldo' products (latest file seen dated 14/04/2026). I did not find the current rule for keeping a balance book on non-ketamine products; it may sit in Decreto 25/2005, which I did not check. Penalty not found.
result.market: No count found. SAG publishes an XLS of 'Establecimientos inscritos para la venta de Ketamina' (updated 23/09/2026); I did not open it, so the number of rows is not known. Registering as a veterinary-medicine seller costs 2 UTM through ChileAtiende procedure 58052. No total count of veterinary-medicine sellers was found.
result.reason: The claim's legal basis is out of date. SAG Res. Ex. 7813, published 14-12-2017 and in force since then, sets the rules for selling veterinary products that contain ketamine. Its title says it repeals Res. 667 and Res. 1816 of 2010 (title seen in search summaries; full text not opened). So the general 667/2010 rules on handwritten prescriptions, the folio register and monthly reporting no longer apply. Under 7813, the monthly entries/exits/balance report due in the first 10 business days appears, from a search summary, in the section for laboratories and importers. I could not confirm that it applies to sellers. The current duty looks limited to ketamine sellers on a short SAG list, which makes the market very small. No software for this was found, but the gap matters little.

result.competitor: The core recurring job is covered. The SII's own e-invoicing portal lets withholding agents issue a factura de compra electronica and pick cambio-de-sujeto products or a 'generico con retencion total' option, which fills in the product and cambio-sujeto codes. The SII publishes the retention codes, so any certified Chilean DTE provider can support this too. I did not confirm how Bsale, Nubox or Defontana configure it, and the portal page does not say whether it is free. For yard operations, foreign scrap software exists, such as ReMatter and ScrapRight on Capterra Chile and Basys from Mexico, but none appeared to be localized for the SII. A Chile-specific scrap ERP would be a vertical tool, not a solution to an unmet compliance duty.
result.duty: The tax duty is real and in force. SII Res. Ex. 86/2016 moves the whole IVA charge on scrap sales to the buyer. Letter d) covers non-exporter, non-manufacturer firms that buy or sell more than CLP 20m net in a month, or buy CLP 150m net in 12 months. Those firms file Anexo 4 (Declaracion Jurada de Agentes Retenedores) and join the nomina. Letter e) lets the SII add smaller yards at its discretion. Regional SII resolutions in 2023-2025 still add yards to the nomina under Res. 86, which shows it is still applied. In practice a withholding agent issues a factura de compra electronica (DTE 46), adds 100% of the IVA as a retention ("IVA RETENIDO CHATARRA", total retention) and declares it monthly. The 'origin documentation and supplier checks' part has no legal mandate behind it. No dealer register exists. Boletin 14.983 (cable theft and receptacion) has been with a Comision Mixta since Jan 2025, according to a CTMIN report, and I found no later enactment. The only risk to yards is criminal liability for receptacion, which is not a recurring workflow. I did not verify the penalty amounts for failing to withhold.
result.market: I found no count. The SII publishes the withholding-agent nomina, but I did not reach it, and no article gave a total. A 2016 DF article reports 428 SII inspections of the scrap trade in 2016 and copper scrap shipments of about 181,000 t. The informal yards described in the claim are mostly below the thresholds and outside the duty. Probably a few hundred obligated firms; this is not verified.
result.reason: The IVA cambio-de-sujeto duty under Res. 86/2016 is real, monthly and in force. But its core task, issuing a factura de compra with total retention and declaring it, already runs through the SII's own e-invoicing portal and standard DTE software. The 'origin documentation and supplier checks' part has no legal mandate: there is no dealer register, and the cable-theft bill was stuck in a Comision Mixta as of the latest source I found (Mar 2025). The obligated firms are a small, unquantified group, likely a few hundred. The informal yards the claim targets are mostly below the thresholds, unlikely to pay, and serving them carries reputational and legal risk around receptacion.

result.competitor: Quimun (Chilean, a 2023 spin-off of DataQu; ELEAM management platform with medical, hotel and admin modules and a family portal; about 15 homes in Chile and 3 in Ecuador). Mera Inn (Chilean electronic clinical records for elder-care homes). Resisoft (Uruguay, in 5 countries). Spanish ResiPlus. None was confirmed to produce Seremi authorisation or inspection packs specifically.
result.duty: Seremi de Salud sanitary authorisation and inspection of ELEAM (old DS 14/2010 regime; Supreme Court upheld closure for operating without authorisation). DS 20/2021 publication date of 30 Sep 2022 confirmed. Its entry into force was postponed several times; the Apr and Jul 2025 Diario Oficial decrees, as summarised in search results, give 1 Apr 2025 and a 3-year transition for existing homes (to about Apr 2028), plus 5 years for smoke detectors under the annual Seremi inspection programme. The decree PDF could not be read to confirm this text. No fixed recurring filing frequency was confirmed. Penalties are sumarios sanitarios, fines and closure. After the Pitrufquen fire (11 Sep 2026, 16 dead, a home without authorisation), the government announced stronger inspection and an intersectoral working group. No new bill or new duty was confirmed.
result.market: Emol/El Mercurio (Sep 2026): about 900 authorised private homes plus 23 public homes (Senama), and an unknown number of clandestine ones. Other sources give 875 to 947. The 2025 network survey says 97% are private.
result.reason: The duty is real. Seremi de Salud authorises and inspects ELEAM, and a Supreme Court ruling confirms closure for operating without authorisation. But DS 20/2021 has been postponed several times. According to the Jul 2025 decree as reported in search results, it applies from 1 Apr 2025, and existing homes only have to comply after 3 years (Apr 2028), so the claim's 'in force 30 Sep 2022' is wrong. The claim also says no ELEAM-specific product exists. That is contradicted by Quimun, a Chilean platform built for ELEAM with medical, hotel and admin modules, used by about 15 homes in Chile. Mera Inn (clinical records for elder-care homes) and Resisoft (Uruguay) also exist. A narrower compliance desk could still have room. About 900 private homes are authorised.

result.competitor: No software built for alcohol-patente renewal found in two searches. Simplo (simplo.cl) has a page for this permit, but it is a generic permit-tracking and advisory service: no published price, it does not file the renewal, and it says it does not replace the authority. ChileAtiende ficha 349 (the Carabineros report) is marked as not available online (from the search snippet; fetching the page returned 403). In the documents seen, municipalities ask for in-person delivery, so there is no state portal that does the job end to end. Local gestores and lawyers almost certainly sell this service, but no pricing was found.
result.duty: Real, but partly reframed. Under Ley 19.925, the patente fee is paid each half-year in advance, in January and July (documented in municipal instructions and SUBDERE prórroga news). Renewal or caducidad is decided by the Concejo Municipal from a list that records: DOM final reception, the holder's criminal record certificate, a notarised sworn statement on the art. 4 inhabilidades, a Carabineros report and the junta de vecinos opinion. Each comuna sets its own deadline and documents. Chillán's deadline for period 1/2026 was 24 Oct 2025, and one 2025 instruction says patentes must be fully paid by 31 Jan and documents handed in in person. Non-renewal or caducidad means losing the licence. Courts are active on renewal refusals (2025-2026 rulings). The bill making the junta de vecinos opinion binding was still pending (Sept 2025 article); not checked whether it passed.
result.market: No national count found in 3 searches. The cap for limited categories (botillerías A, bars E, cervecerías F, minimercados H) is 1 per 600 inhabitants, which gives at most about 32,000 nationwide on roughly 19.5M people. That figure is my own calculation from the legal cap, not a register number. Restaurants and other unlimited categories come on top, so the total is probably a few tens of thousands of patentes across about 345 comunas. Unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real, recurs every six months, and missing it can cost the patente. But most of the work is collecting a criminal record certificate, a notarised statement and the junta and Carabineros steps, then filing in person in each comuna's own format. Software can only remind and give checklists; it cannot file anything. Rules and dates differ across about 345 comunas, so the content is expensive to keep current. Buyers are small, many are cash-based and low-tech, and gestores or accountants already handle it, so there is little room to charge for a calendar. A done-for-you gestoría in one region, such as the Santiago metro area, is more realistic than SaaS. Market size and gestor fees are unverified.
